newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tankers steady, shrug off Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tankers steady, shrug off Iraq.

text.p: The Middle Eastern crude tanker market remained sluggish with rates unchanged, shipping brokers said on Friday. Tension in the region between the U.S. and Iraq was not impacting.
"Because war insurance exists, as yet no one seems to have been frightened off," said a broker.
Both the Western Hemisphere and Asia/Pacific sectors saw rates settle at last done levels, amid thinning activity.
Brokers said VLCC trips to Japan out of the Middle East were unchanged at W57.5, while trips Westwards could command around W48, though as low as low as W46.25 was seen, brokers said.
VLCCs heading for Asia remained around W54.5.
"A number of older units are now running spot and a plethora of their sisters remain unfixed in the month of September," shipbrokers Galbraith's said in a weekly report.
"Many of these ships can surely only entice charterers with cheaper rates than last done," the report concluded.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med settled at W100, as evidenced by Repsol's chartering of the Enalios Triton. But brokers said that as high as W102.5 and as low as W95 was seen.
In the inter-UKC sector rates ascended fractionally to W95 from W92.5, amid a thicker market.
A couple of transatlantic trips were seen with both Total and J.P.Morgan chartering vessels to the US Gulf.
Caribbean rates settled at last done levels, with 70,000 tonners going upcoast-U.S at W147.5.
"Volume in the Caribs sharply increased over the last few days and consequently rates have remained fairly high," a North American broker said.
The tension in the Middle East Gulf had not affected rates in the Middle East.
